title: Selecting with loc and iloc
summary: Columns, label and position slicing, boolean masks and new columns.
intro: A small sales table with a text index (`r1` to `r6`), so label-based `.loc` and position-based `.iloc` give different answers.

tasks.title: One column as a Series
tasks.prompt: Store the `units` column in `units`, as a **Series** (not a one-column DataFrame).
tasks.check:
assert isinstance(units, pd.Series), f"units should be a Series, got {type(units).__name__} (single brackets give a Series, double brackets a DataFrame)"
assert units.tolist() == [12, 7, 3, 15, 9, 4], "units should hold the units column"
assert list(units.index) == ["r1", "r2", "r3", "r4", "r5", "r6"], "keep the original index"
hints: `df['col']` gives a Series; `df[['col']]` gives a DataFrame.

tasks.title: The first three rows by position
tasks.prompt: Store the first three rows (all columns) in `first_three`, selecting **by position** with `.iloc`.
tasks.check:
assert isinstance(first_three, pd.DataFrame), "first_three should be a DataFrame"
assert list(first_three.index) == ["r1", "r2", "r3"], f"expected rows r1, r2, r3, got {list(first_three.index)}"
assert list(first_three.columns) == list(sales.columns), "keep all four columns"
hints: `.iloc` slices exclude the stop position, like Python lists: `[:3]` is positions 0, 1, 2.

tasks.title: A label slice with two columns
tasks.prompt: Store rows `r2` **through** `r4` (inclusive), with only the `region` and `units` columns, in `middle`. Use `.loc`.
tasks.check:
assert isinstance(middle, pd.DataFrame), "middle should be a DataFrame"
assert list(middle.index) == ["r2", "r3", "r4"], f"expected rows r2, r3, r4, got {list(middle.index)} (a .loc slice includes its end label)"
assert list(middle.columns) == ["region", "units"], f"expected columns ['region', 'units'], got {list(middle.columns)}"
hints: `.loc[rows, columns]`: rows can be a label slice `'r2':'r4'`, columns a list of names.
Unlike `.iloc`, a `.loc` slice **includes** the end label.

tasks.title: Filter with a boolean mask
tasks.prompt: Store the rows where `units` is greater than 8 in `big`.
tasks.check:
assert isinstance(big, pd.DataFrame), "big should be a DataFrame"
assert list(big.index) == ["r1", "r4", "r5"], f"expected rows r1, r4, r5, got {list(big.index)}"
hints: `sales['units'] > 8` is a Series of True/False; indexing with it keeps the True rows.

tasks.title: Combine two conditions
tasks.prompt: Store the rows where `region` is `"North"` **and** `product` is `"B"` in `north_b`.
tasks.check:
assert isinstance(north_b, pd.DataFrame), "north_b should be a DataFrame"
assert list(north_b.index) == ["r5"], f"expected only row r5, got {list(north_b.index)}"
hints: pandas uses `&` (and), `|` (or) and `~` (not), not the Python keywords.
Wrap each condition in parentheses: `&` binds more tightly than `==`.

tasks.title: Add a column without changing the original
tasks.prompt:
Make `with_revenue`: a **copy** of `sales` with an extra column `revenue` = `units * price`.
`sales` itself must stay unchanged.
tasks.check:
assert "revenue" not in sales.columns, "sales gained a revenue column: plain assignment (with_revenue = sales) names the same object, so make a copy first"
assert isinstance(with_revenue, pd.DataFrame), "with_revenue should be a DataFrame"
assert "revenue" in with_revenue.columns, "with_revenue needs a revenue column"
assert with_revenue["revenue"].tolist() == [30.0, 28.0, 7.5, 90.0, 36.0, 24.0], "revenue should be units * price for each row"
hints: `df.copy()` makes an independent DataFrame; `b = a` only gives the same object a second name.

tasks.title: The label of the largest value
tasks.prompt: Store the **index label** of the row with the most units in `best` (it should be a label such as `"r1"`, not a position).
tasks.check: assert best == "r4", f"best should be 'r4', got {best!r}" + (" (that is the largest value itself; idxmax gives its label)" if best == 15 else "")
hints: `.max()` gives the value; `.idxmax()` gives the index label where it occurs.
